assessment.verdict: No, it is not handled. There is no per-client invoicing channel anywhere in the codebase, and the thing that looks like one is not one. The Stripe-vs-Xero decision is made fresh on every single invoice by a three-chip picker in the New Invoice slide-over that resets to "Dashboard only" every time it opens (app/(dashboard)/invoices/invoice-list.tsx:227, :261) and never looks at the client. The same dialog hardcodes currency to NZD and ignores organisations.preferredCurrency. Nothing on the client detail page says how a client bills: the Billing card (app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:1244-1330) holds billing model, currency, MRR, hourly rate and retainer dates and stops there. organisations.paymentTerms is the only channel-adjacent column and its own schema comment already reads like a rail ("null / 'card' = card on file via Stripe", db/schema.ts:57-61), yet it is written in exactly one place, hardcoded to net_14 (app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:147), it is not in the client PATCH allowlist (app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts:259-263) and it is not rendered anywhere. The GET already returns it (a bare .select() at :33-36), so the value is on the wire and nobody reads it. organisations.billingModel is not a rail either: it is an auto-derived revenue-shape label whose only non-writer reader in the whole app is the retainer-health report. The two rails are also not equal halves. Stripe is a complete loop: create, finalise, persist the hosted pay URL, email a Pay button, take the card, reconcile by webhook. Xero is a one-way push of a DRAFT that nothing ever approves (Status: 'DRAFT' hardcoded at app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts:189; AUTHORISED appears in the repo only as an incoming status to read, never as a write), so the client never gets a payable Xero page. OnlineInvoiceUrl, the field that would carry Pay now on the Xero side, appears zero times in the repo. Portal payUrl is stripeHostedInvoiceUrl verbatim in all three projections and the CTA subtitle hardcodes "Secure payment page, hosted by Stripe", so a Xero-billed client opens their invoice in the portal and finds nothing to click, no bank details, no reference and no PDF. The AI chase prompt is written around that hole: "DO NOT invent a payment link or bank details." Two money bugs sit on the same path and are half an hour of work between them: the admin invoice GET never selects `source` (route.ts:86-107) so every invoice reads "Manual" on the detail while the list badge reads correctly, and PATCH accepts only status/dueDate/notes/orgId (:86-103) while the UI sends paidAt and sentAt (invoice-detail.tsx:141-146), so hand-marking a bank-transfer invoice paid leaves paid_at NULL, and /financial-reports keys YTD revenue and 90-day collected off paidAt, not status. Separately, the one path that can actually double-bill is CT.13, confirmed: app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts says "for hourly clients" at :13 and applies no billing-model filter at :54-67, has no idempotency guard around the insert, silently `continue`s a zero-rate client at :96-98 and hardcodes NZD at :117 and :146. Its only caller is an MCP tool, which is the only reason it has not burned anyone.
howItWorksToday: Rail is per invoice, not per client. app/(dashboard)/invoices/invoice-list.tsx:227 `useState<'manual'|'xero'|'stripe'>('manual')`, reset to 'manual' on every close at :261, three chips at :362-366, fan-out to /api/admin/invoices/xero-sync or /stripe-create after the draft is created. No effect keyed on the selected org; currency also hardcoded to 'NZD' at :247.

organisations.paymentTerms (db/schema.ts:57-61) already documents itself as a rail-ish field but is write-once from onboarding: the sole writer is app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:147, hardcoded to DEFAULT_INVOICE_TERMS = 'net_14' (lib/invoice-billing.ts:25). Its readers are the onboarding entitlement gate (:129, :303) and the onboarding draft's due date. paymentTermsLabel (lib/invoice-billing.ts:54) has zero dashboard consumers.

The value is already fetched and thrown away: GET /api/admin/clients/[id] does a bare `.select()` over organisations (route.ts:33-36) so paymentTerms is in the payload, but it is absent from the PATCH allowlist (:259-263) and from the client-detail Billing card (client-detail.tsx:1244-1330), so an admin can neither see nor change it.

organisations.billingModel is not a rail. It is auto-derived revenue shape (retainer/hourly/project/none) via lib/billing-derivation.ts, re-derived on every client-detail GET (app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts:41-49), stored outside Drizzle and reached by raw SQL (:55-80 read, :288-294 write). Its only non-writer reader anywhere is app/api/admin/reports/retainer-health/route.ts. Zero reads on the invoice path.

Stripe rail is complete. app/api/admin/invoices/stripe-create/route.ts creates the customer if absent, adds items, finalises at :171, then PERSISTS hosted_invoice_url plus source 'stripe', status 'sent' and first-send sentAt at :179-188, and rings the billing contacts once.

Xero rail is a one-way DRAFT push. xero-sync/route.ts:189 hardcodes Status 'DRAFT' on create and update; on success it writes only xeroInvoiceId and source 'xero' at :236-240, never status and never sentAt. Nothing in the repo ever writes AUTHORISED (grep: AUTHORISED appears only as an incoming case in lib/xero-sync.ts:281,614 and app/api/webhooks/xero/route.ts:129). A Xero draft is not an issued bill, so there is nothing for the client to pay.

The client CTA renders only when payUrl is set and its subtitle says "Secure payment page, hosted by Stripe" (invoice-detail.tsx:317-355). The email forks the same way (emails/invoice-sent.tsx:82-87), degrading to "View invoice".

The system knows the hole: app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/draft-chase/route.ts:61 instructs the model "DO NOT invent a payment link or bank details - Liam adds those on send if needed."

That last number is the size of the revenue hole today.

Neither cross-checks the other's column. proposal.model: Separate the two things paymentTerms is currently trying to be. Keep organisations.paymentTerms as WHEN it is due (card | net_7 | net_14 | net_30, vocabulary already exists in lib/invoice-billing.ts) and add one new column, organisations.invoiceChannel, for HOW it is billed and paid: 'stripe' (Stripe invoice, card, Stripe hosted pay page), 'xero_stripe' (Xero invoice, approved, paid by card through the Stripe payment service on the Xero branding theme) and 'xero_bank' (Xero invoice, approved, paid by bank transfer). NULL means unset and falls back to a studio default in settings, so nothing changes behaviour until Liam names each client. Per invoice, keep invoices.source as the snapshot of the rail actually used ('manual' stays meaningful: raised in the dashboard, not pushed anywhere). Add exactly one new invoice column, invoices.xeroOnlineInvoiceUrl, mirroring the existing stripeHostedInvoiceUrl, and make the three payUrl projections plus resolvePayUrl coalesce the two. Both Xero channels use the same mechanism (Xero's own online invoice page, which carries the bank details from the branding theme and carries Pay now only when Stripe-on-Xero is attached to that theme), so the channel value decides the label and the expectation, not a second plumbing path. That is the whole model: one org column, one invoice column, one coalesce.
proposal.setting: A two-field row in the existing Billing section of the client detail edit form (app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx, next to Currency at :1260-1270): "Invoicing channel" (Stripe card / Xero + card / Xero + bank transfer / Use studio default) and "Payment terms" (Card on file / Net 7 / Net 14 / Net 30, using paymentTermsLabel which already exists and has no consumers). Both go into the PATCH allowlist at app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts:259-263 as ordinary Drizzle columns, so neither needs the raw-SQL billingColumnMap dance that billingModel uses. Underneath, read-only linkage chips showing whether this client has a Stripe customer and a Xero contact, because both can silently exist at once and both auto-backfill on first use. The studio default lives in settings alongside the existing invoice_number_prefix key. MCP parity: add both fields to update_client and create_client, and add the missing xero-sync tool.
proposal.clientSees: stripe: unchanged from today. Pay now on the portal list row, the mobile card and the invoice detail, plus a Pay button in the email, subtitle "Secure payment page, hosted by Stripe". xero_stripe: the same Pay CTA, pointing at the Xero online invoice page, subtitle "Secure payment page, hosted by Xero". xero_bank: no card CTA, but no dead end either: a "How to pay" block on the portal invoice detail and in the email carrying the amount, the due date, the invoice number as the payment reference, and a "View invoice and bank details" link to the Xero online invoice page. An unset channel with no pay URL behaves exactly as today (portal link only), so nothing regresses before the backfill pass.

Sending a Stripe link will create a second customer record."). The invoice detail shows the real Source instead of always "Manual", the channel chip, and, for the Xero rail, whether the invoice is still a draft in Xero. The client list and client detail show the channel so "who is on bank transfer" is answerable at a glance. Worse, the push direction stamps a UUID fragment into the real Xero ledger outside Xero's own sequence, so every day this waits makes the numbering worse. Sequence it before the xero_bank copy reaches clients, or accept that the first bank-transfer emails carry a UUID fragment as the reference.

decisionsForLiam: DRAFT or AUTHORISED: should a dashboard push approve the invoice in Xero (client gets a payable online page immediately, Xero can send its own email with the real PDF and bank details, local status can be trusted) or stay a draft you approve by hand in Xero (ledger stays under your thumb, but the pay link only appears after you act and the dashboard has to poll or wait for the webhook)? This one answer gates the whole Xero pay path, and today's answer is accidentally "draft forever" because nothing in the codebase ever writes AUTHORISED.

Three channels or two? Is xero_bank vs xero_stripe a distinction you want to hold per client, or is it just "Xero" with the branding theme deciding whether Pay now appears? Two values is less to maintain; three lets the portal and the email say the right thing without asking Xero.

Is the Stripe payment service actually attached to the Xero branding theme(s) you use? xero-sync picks a theme by substring-matching the currency code against the theme name (app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts:71-74), so if your themes are not named with NZD/USD/GBP the dashboard's invoices silently get the default theme, which may be the one theme without Stripe on it. Needs one look in Xero.

Backfill by hand or by rule? I would name the channel per client by hand (a ten-minute pass for a book this size) rather than infer it from stripeCustomerId or paymentTerms, since both columns auto-backfill on first use and some orgs may carry both. Say the word if you would rather I write the rule.

Who owns the invoice number on the Xero rail: Tahi's own sequence pushed into Xero, or Xero's sequence mirrored back into the dashboard? It cannot be both, and today it is neither (a UUID fragment goes into the real ledger).

Should a hand mark-paid push back to the rail (mark paid in Xero, void the open Stripe invoice) or stay local-only? Today it is local-only and silent, so a Xero invoice you settled in the bank stays unreconciled in Xero.
Who sends the Xero-rail email: the dashboard (portal link, our template) or Xero (real PDF, real bank details)? Today it can be both, which is two emails for one bill.

Should the hourly export get a UI button after CT.13, and should it refuse any client whose channel is not Xero? Right now it has no button and one MCP caller, which is the only thing standing between it and a double bill.

Should the client ever see their channel named ("You pay by bank transfer, Net 14") in the portal, or is it admin-only context? This decides whether the creation slice needs a portal-side surface at all.

Sequencing: I would run the fixes, the export guard, the column, creation defaults, then numbering, then the pay path, then the status mapper (about 9 days end to end). If you want the client-facing hole closed first, fixes + column + creation + pay path gets there in about 4 days and leaves the export guard and numbering for after, with the caveat that the first bank-transfer emails would carry a UUID fragment as the payment reference.

reads.area: Per-client billing model and the Stripe vs Xero invoicing rail
reads.summary: Short answer to Liam's question: no, this is not handled. There is no per-client invoicing channel anywhere in the codebase. `organisations.billingModel` is not a rail, it is an auto-derived revenue-shape label (retainer/hourly/project/none) that only two files ever read, and neither of them is on the invoice path. The actual Stripe-vs-Xero decision is `invoices.source`, chosen fresh on every single invoice from a badge picker that resets to "manual" each time the create slide-over opens and never pre-fills from the client. Nothing on the client detail page lets you say "this client bills through Xero". The closest existing column, `paymentTerms`, is written in exactly one place (onboarding), hardcoded to net_14, and is not editable by an admin at all. Two consequences bite today: a Xero-rail invoice reaches the portal with no Pay now path (the CTA renders only from `stripeHostedInvoiceUrl`), and `/api/admin/billing/xero-export` claims in its docstring to bill "hourly clients" while applying zero billingModel filter, so it would invoice retainer clients already billed via Stripe. Building a real `invoicingRail` column and threading it through creation, the portal and the export is roughly 2 to 3 days; the CT.13 export guard alone is about 1 to 1.5 days and should land first because it is the only path that can double-bill.
facts: `organisations.billingModel` holds 'retainer' | 'hourly' | 'project' | 'none' (lib/billing-derivation.ts:39). The column is `billing_model text DEFAULT 'none'` added by migration 0016 (app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:127-131 and drizzle/migrations/0016_billing_model_auto_derive.sql:14). It is deliberately NOT in db/schema.ts: the reason is documented at lib/billing-derivation.ts:22-27 and app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts:51-55 (do not add a column to Drizzle until the migration has run on every environment). Every read and write is raw SQL wrapped in try/catch that silently swallows a missing column.

billingModel is auto-derived, not primarily user-set. `deriveBilling` (lib/billing-derivation.ts:138-171) picks the model by precedence: active Stripe subscription -> retainer; customMrr > 0 -> retainer; billable hours in last 60d with no active project -> hourly; active project or won deal with upfront -> project; else none. `applyBillingDerivation` runs on EVERY client-detail GET (app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts:41-49), skipping fields whose `billing_model_is_manual` flag is 1.

Where billingModel is settable: only the client detail edit form. A four-option select (none/retainer/hourly/project) at app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:1249-1259, saved through PATCH /api/admin/clients/[id] which writes it via the raw-SQL `billingColumnMap` at route.ts:288-294 and flips `billing_model_is_manual = 1` at :303-311.

Where billingModel is NOT settable: the client create dialog (app/(dashboard)/clients/client-list.tsx offers only planType, :709-710) and POST /api/admin/clients, whose insert covers only id/name/website/industry/planType/status/healthStatus/timestamps (app/api/admin/clients/route.ts:165-176). Also not settable via MCP: `update_client` (workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts:289-302) exposes name, status, planType, industry, website, internalNotes, customMrr, healthStatus, healthNote, defaultHourlyRate, preferredCurrency, and neither billingModel nor paymentTerms. A grep for billingModel/paymentTerms across workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts returns zero hits. There is no org seed in the repo (only public/seed-docs.json), so no seeded billingModel values exist.

Only two files read billing_model outside its own writer: app/api/admin/reports/retainer-health/route.ts:92 (excludes hourly and project from the retainer report) and lib/billing-derivation.ts itself. `grep -rln billing_model app/api lib` returns 4 files, two of which are the writer and the migration list. Zero reads in invoice creation, the Xero export, the portal, or the MCP server.

There is no invoicing-channel concept. A repo-wide grep for invoiceChannel / invoice_channel / billingChannel / billing_channel / invoiceRail / billingProvider across app, lib, components, workers, db and drizzle returns zero hits. The rail is `invoices.source` ('manual' | 'xero' | 'stripe', db/schema.ts:751), which is per-invoice, not per-client.

The rail is picked per invoice and defaults to manual every time. `destination` state initialises to 'manual' (app/(dashboard)/invoices/invoice-list.tsx:227), is reset to 'manual' on every close of the create slide-over (:261), is rendered as three Badge chips (:415-428), and is never pre-filled from the selected client. POST /api/admin/invoices only records `source` on the draft (route.ts:104-107, :154); the actual push is a separate client-side fetch to /api/admin/invoices/xero-sync or /api/admin/invoices/stripe-create (invoice-list.tsx:309-347).

`paymentTerms` is the closest thing to a per-client billing preference and is nearly write-only. Column `payment_terms text` from migration 0086 (app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:2008-2011); vocabulary card | net_7 | net_14 | net_30 (lib/invoice-billing.ts:22). It is written in exactly ONE place, app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:144-148, and hardcoded to `DEFAULT_INVOICE_TERMS` = 'net_14' (lib/invoice-billing.ts:25). The client cannot pick 7 vs 14 vs 30 (components/tahi/onboarding-payment.tsx:170-178 posts only billingMode/plan/addon/currency), and an admin cannot set or change it at all: paymentTerms is absent from both the `allowed` array (app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts:259-263) and the billingColumnMap (:288-294).

reads.area: Invoices: Xero (bank transfer) vs Stripe (card) channel handling, admin and client surfaces
reads.summary: Short answer: no, it is not handled well. Both rails work individually (Stripe finalise + hosted pay page, Xero draft push + webhook reconcile), but there is no per-client channel anywhere in the data model or the admin UI. Nothing in D1 records "this client pays by bank transfer through Xero" vs "this client pays by card through Stripe". `organisations.paymentTerms` is the closest thing and it only records net terms chosen during self-serve onboarding; it is never displayed or editable on the client detail page. The channel is a per-invoice decision made by whichever button Liam clicks, and the New Invoice dialog defaults to "Dashboard only" every single time regardless of client. The Stripe side is complete end to end. The Xero/bank-transfer side is a dead end for the client: the portal invoice detail and the invoice email contain no bank details, no payment reference, no PDF, and no "how to pay" text at all, and the AI chase prompt explicitly instructs the model not to invent them because the system has none. Two concrete money bugs sit on that same Xero path: marking an invoice paid by hand never stamps `paidAt` (so it never enters YTD revenue or 90-day collected on /financial-reports), and the admin invoice detail never receives `source` from its own API so every invoice reads "Manual" there even when it is a Xero one.
facts: No per-client payment channel exists. db/schema.ts organisations has stripeCustomerId (:40), xeroContactId (:48) and paymentTerms (:61), but no column meaning "bill this client by card" vs "bill this client by bank transfer". Grep for billingModel/billing_model in the main tree returns only client-detail.tsx and app/api/admin/clients/[id]/route.ts, and that field is revenue shape (none | retainer | hourly | project), not a payment rail.

organisations.paymentTerms is the only channel-adjacent signal and it is write-once from onboarding. Its only writer is app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:147 (recordInvoiceMe), its only readers are the same file's entitlement gate (:129, :303) and lib/invoice-billing.ts. It never appears on the admin client detail, so Liam cannot see or change whether a client is on Net 14 or card, and the value it writes is hardcoded to DEFAULT_INVOICE_TERMS = 'net_14' (lib/invoice-billing.ts:24).

The client-detail Billing card has no place for a channel today. app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:1244-1325 renders Billing model, Currency, MRR, Hourly rate, Retainer start/end. There is a natural slot for a "Pay by" selector next to Currency, but nothing is there and paymentTerms is not rendered anywhere in that file.

The channel is chosen per invoice, in the New Invoice dialog, and always defaults to manual. app/(dashboard)/invoices/invoice-list.tsx:227 is `useState<'manual'|'xero'|'stripe'>('manual')` with no effect keyed on orgId; destOptions at :363-367 are Dashboard only / Xero draft / Stripe link. After creation it fans out to /api/admin/invoices/xero-sync (:310) or /api/admin/invoices/stripe-create (:321). So a bank-transfer client can be given a Stripe link and a card client can be pushed to Xero with no guard rail.

The Stripe rail is complete. stripe-create/route.ts finalises the invoice, persists hosted_invoice_url to invoices.stripeHostedInvoiceUrl (:174-176), flips status to 'sent', stamps sentAt once and rings the client bell once. The portal list (app/api/portal/invoices/route.ts:65) and detail (app/api/portal/invoices/[id]/route.ts:78) both project that column as payUrl, and the client gets a real Pay CTA on the list row (invoice-list.tsx:959-970), the mobile card, and the detail (invoice-detail.tsx:317-355). The email leads with it (emails/invoice-sent.tsx:84-86).

The Xero/bank-transfer client sees nothing payable. If stripeHostedInvoiceUrl is null the pay CTA simply does not render, and no alternative is substituted: no bank account number, no payment reference, no due-date instruction, no PDF. emails/invoice-sent.tsx degrades to a "View invoice" button pointing at the portal (:84-86), and that portal page then shows amount, line items, notes and dates only. There is no 'how to pay' block anywhere in either surface.

The studio has no bank details stored to put there even if the UI existed. components/tahi/settings/sections/studio-details.tsx:63-68 saves studio_legal_name, studio_gst_number, studio_address, studio_billing_currency, invoice_number_prefix, invoice_footer_note. There is no bank account / IBAN / reference field, and grep shows zero readers for any of those six keys outside that component, so even invoice_footer_note (the obvious place for payment instructions) is collected and discarded.

The system already knows this gap. app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/draft-chase/route.ts:61 instructs the model: "DO NOT invent a payment link or bank details - Liam adds those on send if needed." The dunning email is written around the absence.

MONEY BUG: Mark as Paid never stamps paidAt. invoice-detail.tsx:145 sends `body.paidAt`, but PATCH /api/admin/invoices/[id] only reads status, dueDate, notes and orgId (route.ts:86-103) and drops paidAt on the floor. The row goes status='paid' with paid_at NULL. app/api/admin/financial-reports/summary/route.ts:513-516 computes YTD revenue from "paidAt set + > yearStart" precisely because Stripe and Xero imports use different status vocabularies, and :698 computes 90-day collected the same way. So every bank-transfer invoice Liam settles by hand is invisible to YTD revenue, collected90 and revenue-per-hour. Stripe-paid and Xero-webhook-paid invoices are unaffected (webhooks/stripe/route.ts:129, webhooks/xero/route.ts:210 both set it). Fix is roughly 15 minutes plus a test.

BUG: the admin invoice detail always says Source: Manual. invoice-detail.tsx:37 declares `source: string | null` as required and :309-312 renders it, but GET /api/admin/invoices/[id] (route.ts:40-60) never selects schema.invoices.source. The admin LIST does select it (app/api/admin/invoices/route.ts:57) and renders a correct SourceBadge, so list and detail disagree about the same invoice. One-line fix.

Xero invoices are pushed as DRAFT and left there. xero-sync/route.ts:189 hardcodes Status: 'DRAFT' on both the create and the update path. Nothing ever moves them to AUTHORISED, so Liam still has to open Xero, approve and send from there. That means two sends for one bill (the dashboard email with a portal link, and Xero's own email with the real PDF and bank details) and the local status ('sent') is set by an email that carried no way to pay.

Marking paid locally does not push back to either rail. PATCH only voids in Xero on written_off (route.ts:129-144). A local mark-paid leaves the Xero invoice unreconciled and the Stripe invoice open. Reconciliation only ever flows inward via the two webhooks.

Asymmetry the audit already flagged and I confirmed: a Xero-paid invoice rings the studio bell (webhooks/xero/route.ts:225-230 notifyAllAdmins) while a Stripe-paid invoice fires a domain event only (webhooks/stripe/route.ts:143-149). Same business event, different loudness depending on the rail.

MCP parity is broken on both channels. There is no xero-sync tool at all in workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts (grep for 'xero-sync' returns nothing), so an assistant can create a Stripe invoice (create_stripe_invoice, :1472) but cannot push one to Xero. Worse, create_invoice (:627) exposes only orgId/amountUsd/totalUsd/notes/dueDate and proxies straight to POST /api/admin/invoices (:1936), which rejects any body without a non-empty lineItems array (invoices/route.ts:115-117). The tool as specified can only ever 400, and it cannot set `source` either.

The hourly Xero export is the trap CT.13 describes and I re-verified it. app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts has no idempotency key, so a second run for the same month creates a second local invoice and a second Xero draft; no billingModel filter despite its docstring (:13), so it invoices every org with billable hours including retainer clients already billed via Stripe; :97-98 falls back to defaultHourlyRate then silently `continue`s a zero-rate client; and :117 hardcodes currency 'NZD' regardless of the org's preferredCurrency. Its only caller anywhere is the MCP tool auto_generate_invoices (index.ts:2538).

Copy Payment Link on the admin detail is a silent no-op for most seats. It calls GET /api/admin/integrations/stripe/provision (invoice-detail.tsx:471) which is gated on the 'settings.integrations' feature (provision/route.ts:119-120) rather than 'invoices', and the button's handler has `if (res.ok) {...}` with no else (:472-481), so a 403 does nothing visible. That route also has no requireAccessToOrg, so a scoped team member can read any invoice's Stripe pay URL by id.

ManyRequests parity, verified live through the ManyRequests MCP rather than from memory: every invoice carries a sequential number (INV-2026000030, INV-2025000024), a payment_url on Tahi's own domain at /invoices/<token>/order for every status including pending, multi-currency amounts (USD/GBP/EUR on real rows), and a status vocabulary that includes 'in progress', documented as "a payment that started outside the portal and is often already paid". That is exactly the bank-transfer state this dashboard has no word for. paid_at is populated on every paid row, including Physitrack GBP 3,125 rows where paid_at equals created_at, i.e. the manual mark-paid pattern that silently loses paidAt here.
gaps: No channel field to build on. Adding one is a schema decision first: extend organisations.paymentTerms into a real vocabulary ('stripe_card' | 'xero_bank' | net terms as a separate column) or add organisations.invoiceChannel alongside it. Either way it needs a Drizzle migration with IF NOT EXISTS reviewed against prod, plus a backfill decision for the ~1 client already carrying net_14. Estimate 0.5d for schema + migration + backfill, then 1d BE/FE for the client-detail Billing card control, defaulting the New Invoice destination from it, and a channel chip on the admin invoice detail. ~1.5-2d total.

Bank-transfer payment instructions do not exist at any layer. Needs studio settings fields (account name, bank/account number, SWIFT/IBAN, reference format), a reader for them (nothing reads any studio_* settings key today), a payment block on the portal invoice detail, and a matching block in emails/invoice-sent.tsx for the no-payUrl branch. Estimate ~1d, and it depends on Liam supplying the actual account details.

No Xero PDF anywhere. lib/xero.ts only exposes JSON helpers (callXeroAPI / callXeroAPIOrThrow); there is no binary variant and zero occurrences of application/pdf against Xero. A Download PDF affordance on both the admin and portal detail needs a new binary fetch path (Xero GET /Invoices/{id} with Accept: application/pdf), an auth-scoped proxy route, and a decision on caching to R2 vs streaming per request. Estimate ~1d. Note the audit already records "No PDF download exists anywhere in the invoices UI".

The Xero DRAFT-vs-AUTHORISED question is a Liam decision I cannot make: does the dashboard authorise and send from Xero (one email, real PDF, real bank details, real Xero invoice number) or keep pushing drafts and let Liam finish in Xero (status divergence, two emails)? Everything about the Xero client experience hangs off that answer. Roughly 0.5-1d of BE once decided.

Invoice numbering (CT.14) blocks the bank-transfer story more than it blocks the Stripe one: a bank transfer needs a stable reference the client puts in their payment, and today identity is three different UUID slices (invoice-detail.tsx:186 slice(0,6), :254 slice(0,8), xero-sync/route.ts:215 slice(0,8)) while invoice_number_prefix is collected and never read. The 2.5d estimate in TASKS.md looks right and I would sequence it before the payment-instructions work, not after.

I did not verify any of this live. Read-only session, no browser, no dev server. In particular I have not confirmed what a real Xero-only client currently sees in the deployed portal, nor whether the Xero webhook is actually registered on prod (app/api/webhooks/xero/route.ts:45 describes a manual setup step in the Xero app's Webhooks tab).

I did not check whether Stripe-on-Xero (Liam's note that Stripe is connected to Xero) creates duplicate ledger rows when an invoice is both Stripe-finalised and Xero-synced. That is a real risk given both stripeInvoiceId and xeroInvoiceId can be set on the same row and nothing prevents it, but confirming it needs the live Xero ledger, not the code.

I did not audit lib/stripe-import.ts, lib/stripe-sync.ts or lib/xero-sync.ts in depth, nor the import routes under integrations/*/import-invoices. They matter for the migration story (importing historical ManyRequests/Xero invoices) but not for the channel question Liam asked.

reads.area: Invoice creation, sync and payment paths (Stripe vs Xero)
reads.summary: Both rails exist and both work, but they are not two halves of one system. Stripe is a complete loop: create, finalise, persist a hosted pay URL, email a Pay button, take the payment, reconcile by webhook. Xero is a one-way push: an invoice goes out as a DRAFT, gets a UUID-derived invoice number stamped into Liam's real Xero ledger, and comes back with no pay link, no number, no sentAt and no reliable status. Answering the question directly: the Stripe-vs-Xero choice is NOT a client setting. It is a radio in the New Invoice slide-over that defaults to "manual" every time it opens, so today it is a per-invoice decision Liam has to remember for each client rather than a per-client default the system enforces. And OnlineInvoiceUrl (the Xero-hosted page that carries Pay now when Stripe is connected on the Xero side) appears nowhere in the repo: no column, no fetch, no UI. The portal's payUrl is stripeHostedInvoiceUrl verbatim and the CTA copy hardcodes "hosted by Stripe", so a Xero-billed client sees their invoice in the portal with no way to pay it. Underneath that, three separate Xero-to-local status mappers disagree with each other, the Xero import refuses to update rows it has already seen, and the nightly Stripe import silently reverts any invoice a human or the payment_failed webhook marked overdue.
facts: EIGHT doors mint an invoice row. Manual: POST /api/admin/invoices (app/api/admin/invoices/route.ts:79-192, always status 'draft', source = the operator's stated intent). Stripe push: app/api/admin/invoices/stripe-create/route.ts (creates customer if absent, creates + finalises the Stripe invoice, persists stripeInvoiceId AND stripeHostedInvoiceUrl, sets source 'stripe', status 'sent', stamps sentAt, raises the client bell). Xero push: app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts. Hourly export: app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts:113. Stripe bulk/cron import + webhook self-heal: lib/stripe-import.ts importStripeInvoice. Stripe charge import: lib/stripe-sync.ts importStripePayments (charge id stored in stripeInvoiceId, status 'paid'). Xero import: lib/xero-sync.ts importXeroInvoices:627. Onboarding 'invoice me': app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:186-212 (source 'manual', draft, due date from paymentTerms).

THERE IS NO PER-CLIENT INVOICE PROVIDER SETTING. The destination is React state in the New Invoice slide-over: app/(dashboard)/invoices/invoice-list.tsx:227 declares `useState<'manual'|'xero'|'stripe'>('manual')`, :261 resets it to 'manual' on every close, and :363-366 renders the three options. Nothing reads the client to pick a default. organisations carries stripeCustomerId, xeroContactId, paymentTerms, preferredCurrency and billingModel (db/schema.ts:28-93) and none of them route an invoice anywhere.

organisations.paymentTerms is written by exactly one caller, app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:147, and only when the client self-selects 'invoice me' during onboarding. There is no admin editor for it: the client detail Billing block (app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:1244-1310) offers billing model, currency, MRR, hourly rate and retainer dates, and stops there. stripeCustomerId and xeroContactId are never shown on the client page at all.

OnlineInvoiceUrl does not exist anywhere in the repository (grep across .ts/.tsx/.sql/.md/.json returns zero hits). Both portal routes project payUrl directly off the Stripe column: app/api/portal/invoices/route.ts (payUrl: schema.invoices.stripeHostedInvoiceUrl) and app/api/portal/invoices/[id]/route.ts. The client Pay CTA is gated on it and its subtitle hardcodes 'Secure payment page, hosted by Stripe' (app/(dashboard)/invoices/[id]/invoice-detail.tsx:317, :352). The invoice email's Pay button only renders when paymentUrl is present, otherwise it degrades to 'View invoice' (emails/invoice-sent.tsx:82-83). Net effect: a Xero-billed client has no pay path in the portal or the email.

The reason a Xero pay link cannot exist today even if the column were added: dashboard-pushed invoices are created in Xero with Status 'DRAFT' and never approved (app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts:189, app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts:142). Nothing in the codebase ever moves a Xero invoice to AUTHORISED. A Xero draft is not issued, so Xero has not emailed it and has no online invoice page for it.

The cheapest capture point already exists and is already fetching the right shape. app/api/webhooks/xero/route.ts does a per-invoice GET /Invoices/{id} inside reconcilePayload, which is the Xero call that returns OnlineInvoiceUrl. The bulk importer uses the LIST endpoint instead (lib/xero-sync.ts:630, `/Invoices?where=Type=="ACCREC"&order=DateString DESC&page=N&summaryOnly=false`), so it would need a second per-invoice call.

THREE Xero-to-local status mappers disagree. lib/xero-sync.ts:610 mapXeroStatus maps SUBMITTED to 'sent'. lib/xero-sync.ts:281-289 (syncXeroPayments) maps SUBMITTED to 'viewed' and AUTHORISED to 'sent'. app/api/webhooks/xero/route.ts mapStatus maps SUBMITTED to 'sent' and additionally treats a zero AmountDue on a positive Total as 'paid'. The same Xero invoice therefore reads 'viewed' or 'sent' depending on which job touched it last. 'viewed' also already means something else entirely: the portal detail read stamps viewedAt on first real client open (app/api/portal/invoices/[id]/route.ts).

The Xero import never reconciles anything it has already seen. lib/xero-sync.ts:655 does `if (existingIds.has(inv.InvoiceID)) { skipped++; continue }`. So a Xero invoice imported while DRAFT stays local 'draft' forever, and while it is 'draft' the portal hides it from both the list and the detail (`ne(schema.invoices.status, 'draft')` in both portal routes). The Stripe importer does the opposite and updates in place (lib/stripe-import.ts, existing-row branch).

syncXeroPayments is structurally capped at one page. lib/xero-sync.ts:255 calls `GET /Invoices?ApiKey=` with no page parameter and no status filter, so it only ever sees Xero's first 100 invoices; every local invoice beyond that reports 'not_found_in_xero'. It also stamps paidAt = now rather than Xero's FullyPaidOnDate, which both importXeroInvoices and the Xero webhook use correctly.

The nightly Stripe cron reverts overdue. lib/stripe-import.ts sets `status: localStatus` unconditionally on the existing-row branch, and mapStripeStatus('open') returns 'sent'. POST /api/admin/cron/sync-stripe runs importStripeInvoices daily at 15:00 UTC (.github/workflows/dashboard-crons.yml:44-46). So an invoice the payment_failed webhook marked 'overdue' (app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:168), or that an admin marked 'paid' by hand ahead of Stripe, is silently reset to 'sent' the next morning.

Nothing ever ages an invoice into 'overdue' on its own. The only writer is the Stripe invoice.payment_failed webhook (app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:168). There is no due-date sweeper, so every Xero and every net-terms invoice sits at 'sent' past its due date. That stored status is exactly what the receivables consumers read: app/api/admin/cron/finance-anomaly-scan/route.ts:199, app/api/admin/health/route.ts:137, and the chase gate at app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/draft-chase/route.ts:170 which refuses anything not 'sent' or 'overdue'.

xero-sync never touches local status or sentAt. On success it writes only xeroInvoiceId and source 'xero' (app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts:236-240). So an invoice pushed to Xero, then approved and emailed from inside Xero, is still local 'draft': invisible in the client portal, and invisible to receivables aging, which reads sentAt.

There is no invoices.number column (db/schema.ts:741-779; migration 0086 added only stripe_hosted_invoice_url and payment_terms). Xero's real InvoiceNumber survives only inside a notes string (`Imported from Xero: ${inv.InvoiceNumber}`), Stripe's likewise. Everything user-facing uses invoiceReference() = the first 8 chars of the UUID (lib/invoice-billing.ts). Worse, the push direction stamps that UUID fragment INTO Xero: `xeroPayload.InvoiceNumber = 'INV-' + invId.slice(0,8).toUpperCase()` (app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts, create branch), so dashboard-originated invoices land in the real ledger outside Xero's own numbering sequence. This is TASKS.md CT.14 and is a reason to do it before more invoices are pushed.

The hourly Xero export has no idempotency guard and no billingModel filter, matching TASKS.md CT.13. app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts selects every billable time entry in the month across every org (no billingModel = 'hourly' predicate despite the docstring), and inserts a fresh invoice at :113 with no check for an existing invoice for that org and month. Running it twice for the same month double-bills. It cannot be made idempotent by marking the source rows either: time_entries has no invoiceId or invoicedAt column (db/schema.ts:800-828). It also hardcodes currency 'NZD' at :120 and CurrencyCode 'NZD' at :146, ignoring organisations.preferredCurrency.

Two Xero write routes skip team access scoping. app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts and app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts call requireFeature but never requireAccessToOrg, unlike every sibling money route (app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/route.ts:33, :114, :195; stripe-create; send-email). xero-sync accepts a bare { orgId } and enumerates that org's invoices with no ownership check, so a scoped seat can push any client's invoices to Xero.

MCP parity gap (CLAUDE.md rule 14). workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts exposes create_stripe_invoice (:1472), import_xero_invoices (:1457), sync_xero_payments (:1458) and auto_generate_invoices (:1465, proxying xero-export) but has NO tool for /api/admin/invoices/xero-sync. There is no way to push an invoice to Xero via MCP. Separately, create_invoice (:627-633) does not accept a `source` argument, so an MCP-created invoice can only ever be 'manual'.

stripe-create finalises but never calls POST /invoices/{id}/send (the only Stripe calls are /customers, /invoices, /invoiceitems, /invoices/{id}/finalize at :121, :150, :160, :171). With collection_method 'send_invoice' the invoice sits open in Stripe with no Stripe-side email or reminder cadence; the dashboard's own send-email route is the sole delivery. That is a defensible decision but it means Stripe's dunning is off.

invoices.airwallexTxnId, reconciliationStatus and lastReconciledAt are documented in db/schema.ts:765-772 as multi-source reconciliation feeding the anomaly strip, but nothing writes reconciliationStatus on the invoices table. The only 'orphan' write is to airwallexTransactions, a different table (app/api/admin/integrations/airwallex/sync/route.ts:157). Only the Xero webhook writes lastReconciledAt. The 'Stripe says paid but no Airwallex deposit' story does not exist in code.

The Xero branding theme picker is a substring match on the theme name: `themes.find(t => t.Name.toUpperCase().includes(cur))` (app/api/admin/invoices/xero-sync/route.ts:71-74). If Liam's Xero themes are not named with the currency code, every pushed invoice silently gets Xero's default theme, which is also where the Stripe 'Pay now' payment service is configured per theme.
Minor: stripe-create calls requireFeature twice with identical arguments (app/api/admin/invoices/stripe-create/route.ts:37 and :42), a wasted DB round trip on every call.

Minor: an invoice created with source 'stripe' whose stripe-create then fails keeps source 'stripe' with no stripeInvoiceId, so the list badge (invoice-list.tsx:70-76, SourceBadge) reads 'Stripe' for a row that has no Stripe presence. The retry affordance exists (invoice-detail.tsx:432 shows 'Create Stripe Link' when stripeInvoiceId is null) but the badge is a lie until it is used.
gaps: I could not verify against the live Xero API whether OnlineInvoiceUrl is returned for a DRAFT invoice or only once it is AUTHORISED. My reading of the code path is that it does not matter yet because nothing approves the invoice, but the exact approval trigger to build should be confirmed with one live Xero round trip before writing the fetch.

Whether the Xero webhook is actually live in production. app/api/webhooks/xero/route.ts rejects every delivery with 401 when XERO_WEBHOOK_KEY is unset, and I cannot read production env. If it is not registered, ALL Xero status reconciliation is running through the first-page-only syncXeroPayments, which would make the status drift far worse than the code alone suggests.
Whether the daily sync-stripe and sync-xero crons are actually green in production. Both write to the cron_runs table via logCronRun; I cannot query D1 read-only from here.

Real production data shape: how many invoice rows currently carry xeroInvoiceId vs stripeInvoiceId vs neither, and how many Xero-linked invoices are sitting at local 'draft' (and therefore invisible to the client). That number decides whether the missing Xero pay link is a theoretical gap or is hitting clients this week.

Whether Stripe-on-Xero is enabled on the specific Xero branding theme(s) in use. The theme match is a name substring, and payment services attach per theme, so it is possible for the Pay now button to be missing from exactly the invoices the dashboard pushes even after the URL is captured.

Liam's bookkeeping preference: should a dashboard push auto-approve the invoice in Xero (AUTHORISED), or should it stay a draft he approves in Xero by hand? That is a business decision, not a code one, and it gates the whole OnlineInvoiceUrl design. Auto-approve gives the client a pay link immediately; manual approve keeps his ledger under his thumb but means the pay link only appears after he acts, and the dashboard has to poll or wait for the webhook.
No live browser or dev server was used (read-only brief), so none of the UI behaviour above was exercised; all of it is read from source.
